sources.title: Korea Electronic Travel Authorization (K-ETA)
sources.publisher: Korea Immigration Service, Ministry of Justice
sources.officialityEvidence: The Ministry of Justice immigration site publishes the page and links both the official K-ETA site and the Republic of Korea Visa Portal.
sources.supportingExcerpt: K-ETA is a system for nationals eligible for visa-free entry.

sources.title: Visa Navigator
sources.publisher: Korea Visa Portal, Korea Immigration Service
sources.officialityEvidence: The Ministry of Justice K-ETA page links visa.go.kr as the Republic of Korea Visa Portal. The live Navigator exposes a nationality, short-visit purpose and stay-duration query, but returns purpose/category results rather than a simple nationality-wide complement.

sources.title: K-ETA Application Guide
sources.publisher: Korea Immigration Service, Ministry of Justice
sources.officialityEvidence: The page footer identifies the Korea Electronic Travel Authorization Center and Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Korea.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Nationals eligible for K-ETA, who wish to enter the Republic of Korea without a visa, must obtain K-ETA approval.

unresolved.reason: The current official Visa Navigator requires nationality, purpose and duration inputs and returns mixed visa categories together with narrowly conditional B-1/B-2 transit or document-based no-visa routes; it is not an explicit ordinary-passport advance-visa complement. Its live result text also retains COVID-era suspension wording. The current K-ETA guidance only governs nationals already eligible to enter without a visa, and the 2026 temporary K-ETA exemption is not itself visa-free status. No current MFA, Immigration or Visa Portal rule explicitly assigns this ordinary passport a short-visitor visa requirement or another unconditional category.
